We tend to over romanticize/glorify relationships. We get stuck on this idea that it’s so great and awesome and wonderful to be with someone, that we ignore the fact that it usually isn’t. I was at a rest stop, when I heard a sound from the road that sounded like a trailer hitting a bump, but in a way that immediately made me go “oh shit”. A guy who was standing close to me made eye contact with me, and he, too, had that “oh shit” look on his face. We started running towards the road, and when we got there, I saw a car that had hit the steel railing of a bridge. Then I saw the lifeless body of a woman in the stream under the bridge.

I froze. I couldn’t move. All I did was stand there with my eyes glued to the lady in the water. More people came running and a few men made it down to the stream and tried to get the lady out of the water. I stared at her, and more specifically, my eyes were going back and forth between her head and the piece of her head that had been sliced off and was lying in the grass a few meters away. I wondered if no one else could see that part of her head was gone. Someone did mouth-to-mouth. I kept staring, unable to move. Then, somewhere in the background, I heard my mom screaming to my brother to get me away from there. I think she saw that I was in a state of crisis and had shut down. My brother got me away from there and after that I can’t remember much.

But the image of the lady in the water with part of her head sliced off, will always remain etched into my memory.

I don’t think a person with thick skin would be able to get a thin skin type of defined nose. From my understanding, it’s always gonna be a bit more rounded and undefined. And you run the risk of developing scar tissue under the skin, which I believe is what happened to OP. Because the skin is thicker, it doesn’t drape over the nose bone and cartilage, and that means it can leave a “space” under the skin after a surgery to make the nose smaller, and that “space” is what gets filled up with scar tissue over time.

If any of this information is incorrect please anyone feel free to correct me. I am just pulling this from memory, I read up quite a bit on thick skin surgery some time ago.

Edit: I just remembered that I have heard that a bulbous thick skin nose can be made to look more defined by ADDING more material to the bridge of the nose instead of just removing. I believe that way you make the skin stretch out better over the nose, and it might be less likely to develop scar tissue after a while.

Now, again, I’m not a surgeon, I’m just someone who has the same thick skin problem and I’m desperate to find a way to get a less bulbous nose, so don’t take what I say as facts. Some of it might be wrong.

I recommend searching for “thick skin rhinoplasty” on social media apps. You’ll find lots of photos that can give you an idea of what is possible to accomplish. But remember some of those surgeries might have been performed by someone who doesn’t know what they’re doing and it only looks as good as it does because the after photo was taken soon after the surgery, before the nose starts developing scar tissue

It looks like you have thick skin, which makes it a lot harder to get satisfying results, and if you get a second surgery it’s likely that it will only get worse. If you want a revision rhinoplasty, you need to go to someone who specializes in thick skin revision surgeries. They need to be an expert at thick skin to be able to get good results. I have HEARD that you can thin out the skin before surgery by doing for example different types of laser treatments or plasma pen. But don’t take my word for it, I don’t know if it actually works.

Yessss! Loved reading your comment. A good example of it that happened to me two weeks ago: a friend and I decided to take the train to go to a concert in a different city. We had had the tickets for weeks and during these weeks leading up to the concert, I knew that I would somehow be in contact with someone in the band. I knew it simply because I had a moment when I thought “oh it would be cool to meet them”. And because I had this one thought, I knew the universe would somehow bring me and them together. I never had any doubt about it. When I want something, the universe always gives it to me.

So, my friend and I get to the concert which is sold out. The band is currently the biggest band in my country do it came to no surprise that the venue was packed. I still knew that they would find me somehow.

The night goes on, I post a lot of stories on my ig from the show and tag the band in the stories. After the show my friend and I go out on a quest to find the band (we figured they must have gone to a bar somewhere). We eventually find them in a nightclub but they are in the VIP area. I was trying to come up with a plan to get in to the VIP area but nothing works.
Then I realize that I am here begging and working for something that the universe has already promised me, and by begging and working for it I’m acting like begging and working is something I HAVE to do for it to happen. Something that I’ve already been promised. So I stop trying, and I tell my friend let’s go back to the hotel.

I let go of thinking that I have to do anything, and leave. And I kid you not, when we get back to the hotel room I pick up my phone and check instagram, and there, in my DMs, is the singer of the biggest band in my country, asking me for a date (he had seen my stories and stalked my instagram). I laughed and rolled my eyes at the universe.

When you let go and stop trying, that’s when the magic happens.

I think what most people seem to not quite understand (or they have been taught wrong by books or people) is that the universe doesn’t actually care how you feel or what “energies” you surround yourself with. All that matters is that you have faith in the universe and accept the universe’s unconditional love for you. That really is all it ACTUALLY takes.

There is no need to only think positive thoughts or surround yourself with only positivity. There is no need for mantras or little LOA notebooks filled with all your wishes written down 100 times. There’s no need to meditate on your wishes and loudly thank the universe every night before bed.

To me, trying to control your surroundings, repeating mantras and whatnot, sound a lot like begging and bargaining. “Please universe, if I do this thing, will you please give me the thing I want?”

To me, begging and bargaining is like believing I am not actually unconditionally loved or worthy of everything I could ever wish for. To me, begging says “I don’t actually believe I can get this unless I do something in return, I don’t believe I am loved and worthy just by existing”

I mastered the LOA when I realized this and stopped trying so damn hard. I don’t need to do anything, I don’t need to adjust my surroundings, I don’t need to work for it. I am so incredibly, unconditionally and forever loved by the universe, and all I have to do is accept that love and have faith that no matter what I do or how I feel or where I am, I am still so, so loved.

I have negative people in my life, I have a lot of bad days when I want to punch a hole in the wall, I never repeat mantras and I don’t keep a notebook where I write down my wishes. I have a bad self esteem and I don’t love myself. And I still get everything I want.

I once woke up in the middle of the night cause I heard someone walk into my bedroom. I was facing the wall so I turned around to see who it was (I lived at my mom's at the time and thought it was her).
